deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). X is a stratified space with closed stratum Y and open stratum X* = X \ Y. U*_{Y,X} is the punctured tubular neighbourhood (the link), and diagram (7) is the span Y <- U* -> X*. Grothendieck has built a 'stratified topos' F from the fundamental groups of the pieces (diagrams (8)/(10)). F is a recollement (Artin gluing) of the classifying topoi B_{pi1(Y)} and B_{pi1(X*)} along the specialization data through B_{pi1(U*)}. Concretely, an object of F is a pi1(Y)-set E_Y, a pi1(X*)-set E_{X*}, and a pi1(U*)-equivariant map between their restrictions to pi1(U*). This is the 1-categorical, constructible-sheaf / exit-path picture.

Previous page. For X = C with Y = {a}, F is equivalent to presheaves on a category with a final object. So F is contractible, which is correct because C is contractible.

This page: the test case X = P^1_C ≅ S^2, Y = {∞}, X* = C, U* = D*_∞ ≃ S^1. The diagram of fundamental groups (23) is 1 <- Z -> 1. Since both groups receiving Z are trivial, the Z-equivariance condition is vacuous. An object of F is then just a map of sets E_Y -> E_{X*}, so F ≃ presheaves on C = (• -> •). That category has a final object, so F is homotopically trivial, whereas X = S^2 is not.

Yet all three pieces are K(pi,1)'s ({∞} and C are even contractible, D*_∞ ≃ S^1 = K(Z,1)). Conclusion: a topos that 'in principle takes account of' the pi_1 of the building blocks Y, X*, U* does not necessarily give the homotopy type of X, even when every piece is a K(pi,1). Likewise the canonical morphism (24) X -> F is not necessarily a homotopy equivalence.

Diagnosis in modern terms. The homotopy pushout of the K(pi,1)'s, pt <- BZ -> pt, is ΣS^1 = S^2, which is correct. The 1-topos recollement, however, is an oriented/lax gluing in which the Z-data collapses. This is because the gluing functor factors through 1-categorical invariants/restriction. Equivalently, the exit-path 1-category of (S^2, {∞}) is • -> •, since pi_0 of the exit-path space ≃ S^1 is a point; its classifying space is a point. One must keep the hom-space S^1 at least as a 1-type BZ, i.e. pass to an exit-path 2-category or ∞-category, or to constructible stacks.

The next page indeed says the fear was unfounded. Grothendieck proposes recovering H^2(S^2, A) by interpreting it as classifying A-gerbes and gluing gerbes (a 'recollement' theory for gerbes over topoi). That is a move from sheaves to stacks, exactly the remedy later formalized in the theory of constructible stacks and exit-path higher categories.
errors: Notational slip: the topos is written as script T in 'T ≃ Ĉ' but as F elsewhere; they are the same object.

No mathematical error. The claims are correct: presheaves on a category with a final object are homotopically trivial; the pieces are K(pi,1)'s; S^2 is not trivial. So X -> F is not a homotopy equivalence in this example.
The final sentence is grammatically garbled ('ni d'ailleurs ... le morphisme canonique ... n'est pas nécessairement'), but the meaning is clear.

ideas.what: The topos of a stratified space built by gluing the classifying topoi of pi_1 of strata along the pi_1 of the link (a 1-truncated recollement). Computed for S^2 = C ∪ {∞}, it gives presheaves on • -> •.
ideas.modern_name: Exit-path 1-category / constructible sheaves as representations of the exit-path category; Artin gluing of topoi
ideas.usually_credited_to: Exit-path category: MacPherson (unpublished, 1990s), Treumann (2009), Woolf (2009); Artin gluing: SGA4 (Artin/Grothendieck/Verdier)
ideas.where_published: Gluing of topoi is in SGA4 IV §9. Stratified 'dévissage' is programmatically mentioned in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5-6. This stratified-topos construction itself is not published as far as I know.

ideas.what: Counterexample: even when all strata and links are K(pi,1), the pi_1-based glued topos need not have the homotopy type of X. Example: S^2 with a point stratum gives a contractible topos.
ideas.modern_name: Failure of the classifying space of the exit-path 1-category to recover the homotopy type; need for exit-path ∞-categories (localization recovers Π_∞(X))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Treumann 2009, Woolf 2009; Lurie HA Appendix A; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (∞-categorical exit paths)

ideas.what: Homotopy type of X as homotopy pushout of Y <- U* -> X* (here pt <- S^1 -> pt = S^2), contrasted with the oriented/lax gluing that the topos realizes.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy pushout vs. oriented (lax) pushout / mapping cylinder of topoi

ideas.what: Proposed remedy (on the next page): recover H^2(X, A) through gluing of A-gerbes, i.e. pass from sheaves to stacks/gerbes in the stratified recollement.
ideas.modern_name: Constructible stacks / exit-path 2-category (Treumann); recollement for stacks
ideas.where_published: Gerbes: Giraud (1971); Grothendieck's general programme of ∞-stacks: Pursuing Stacks (1983)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly observes that the 1-topos (exit-path 1-category) of a stratified space loses the homotopy type, with S^2 = C ∪ {∞} as a minimal counterexample. He immediately turns to gerbe/stack gluing to repair it. This links his stratified-topos programme directly to the need for higher stacks, a motivation not usually cited for Pursuing Stacks, and it anticipates the 2-categorical and ∞-categorical exit-path results of Treumann and Lurie by decades.
missed.quote: le topos F, qui en principe semblait "tenir compte" des π_1 des "pièces de construction" Y, X*, U*_{Y,X}, ne donne pas nécessairement le type d'homotopie de X, même si les "morceaux" sont des K(π,1)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly historical: it documents an independent, early recognition that stratified homotopy theory requires higher-categorical gluing data. The example itself is folklore to specialists today.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a simple, correct counterexample that is now folklore in exit-path theory (the constructible sheaves on (S^2, pt) are representations of • -> •). Its interest is historical: an early, unpublished recognition by Grothendieck that pi_1-level gluing of strata fails and that gerbes/stacks are needed, plausibly feeding into Pursuing Stacks. It contains no new theorem.
transcription_corrections: '$\mathbb{Z}^*_{2,2} \simeq \mathbb{D}^*_\infty$' should almost certainly read '$U^*_{Y,X} \simeq \mathbb{D}^*_\infty$' (the handwritten U with subscript Y,X was misread).
'$\{a\}$' is probably '$\{\infty\}$' (Y = {∞} on the previous page), though possibly '{a}' carried over from the earlier example.
'$\mathcal{T} \simeq \hat{C}$' is in Grothendieck's hand a script letter that should be F (the topos F); the leading crossed-out word is illegible.
Diagram (23) on this page is the pi_1 diagram 1 <- Z -> 1, with Z = pi_1(D*_∞) mapping to pi_1(D_∞) = 1 and pi_1(C) = 1.
Last lines: 'ni d'ailleurs le morphisme canonique (24) X -> F n'est [pas] nécessairement une équivalence d'homotopie'.
'qui en principe semblait "tenir compte" des π_1 des "pièces de construction"' is read correctly; the overline word above 'le type d'homotopie' appears to be 'nécessairement'.
